newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends lower in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends lower in line with JGBs.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract settled lower on Wednesday, as sentiment was depressed by a fall in Japanese government bonds and a rise in share prices, traders said.

Comments by Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura that the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) current low interest rate policy is still having positive effects on the economy triggered some buying, but the overall impact was limited, traders said.
Komura's comments simply confirmed the market's view on interest rates and the impact on the market was short-lived, a city bank trader said.
"The upside remained heavy at 99.19/20," he said.
The March's day session turnover was 56,573 contracts.
The Bank of Japan drained 200 billion yen from the money market on Wednesday, against a projected fund surplus of 290 billion yen.
The BOJ's decision to reduce the amount of fund surplus left in the market to about 100 billion yen from about 200 billion yen on Tuesday, came as a mild surprise to the market.
However, the key overnight call rate declined despite the BOJ's surprise move, traders said.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate is likely to be 0.49 percent or 0.48 percent on Wednesday, down from 0.50 percent on Tuesday, they said.

Banks have been able to pile up funds to meet the required amount of reserves rather smoothly during the current bank reserve reporting period, which may account for the decline in the key rate on Wednesday, traders said.
They said the BOJ may decide to conduct a neutral money market operation on Thursday.
"The key overnight call rate may weaken even if the BOJ conducts a neutral operation tomorrow," a trader for another city bank said.
About 40 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) had been issued at 0.61 percent as of 0739 GMT.
About 100 billion yen worth of one-month CDs had been issued at 0.55 percent, while two-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.62 percent.
